objective: Retain the exact resolved worker identity and prevent named external workers from claiming tasks assigned to another runner.

cases: priority ordering among eligible tasks only
persisted task lease and claim event identity

latency.measurement_basis: tool-reported local test duration on the development host

failures.failure: The worker client sent worker identity in the documented query parameter while the Go handler read only the JSON body, so an empty body recorded gateway-worker.
failures.resolution: Resolve a trimmed worker from query or body, reject conflicting non-empty identities, and send the same identity in both client locations for mixed-version compatibility.

failures.failure: The Go task store selected the highest-priority queued task without checking its assigned agent.
failures.resolution: Filter each queued task by the resolved worker before comparing priority, while retaining explicit empty, any, and internal-worker eligibility.

failures.failure: The host Python did not have pytest installed.
failures.resolution: Run the existing four-test compatibility file through an isolated uv environment on the configured cache tier; no global package state changed.

failures.failure: The active-user audit exits one because existing global skills and always-loaded instruction files exceed the configured size budgets.
failures.resolution: No out-of-scope user configuration was changed; all change-relevant contract, hook, profile, installer, provider, and schema checks passed.

reproduction: GOCACHE=<external-cache>/go-build GOMODCACHE=<external-cache>/go-mod GOPATH=<external-cache>/go go -C services/gateway-go test . -run '^TestAgentTask' -count=1 -timeout 120s

rollback.source: revert the worker identity retention commit
rollback.state: existing queued task files remain schema-compatible; no migration is required
